text:
Hi Piyush,

You can find an example of the labeling inconsistencies in change detection
that I mentioned.

   - Sample 1
   <https://app.encord.com/label_editor/61a93776-3d1d-41e1-bdd0-b06edc9f2494/acfd55db-605d-43c5-b3df-6e5b03d60706?selectedStageUuid=50417ebe-7618-4e02-95be-52cec1ccae06&tileFrames=0%3A0%2C1%3A0&activeTileDataHash=767dd24b-bb5b-4c67-8326-cd5cafe7f0f2>
   - Sample 2
   <https://app.encord.com/label_editor/61a93776-3d1d-41e1-bdd0-b06edc9f2494/424a93bf-3a49-40b4-a654-3d86a9cc56f7?selectedStageUuid=50417ebe-7618-4e02-95be-52cec1ccae06&tileFrames=0%3A0%2C1%3A0&activeTileDataHash=09cad682-3940-401a-ad82-ea64d0b3cec3>

As I mentioned in our call, we are currently figuring out a solution that
provides better context to the annotators regarding change detection.
Hopefully we will be able to provide a clearer workflow soon.
In the meantime, it would be great if the annotators could align their
level of detail to achieve rough consistency.

As agreed, I will reduce the number of reviews routed to us to 20% later
today. With that, I request that annotators be more proactive in asking
questions whenever they feel unsure of something, instead of making
assumptions and annotating. We will use our best efforts to clarify any
uncertainties.
It would be great to keep this mode until we roll out a rejection
mechanism, allowing annotators to reject unclear tasks so those tasks land
on our plate for feedback.
I will keep you updated on that.
Let me know if you have any questions.
Thank you.

Best,
Yi Hao

As discussed today, sounds like three things are slowing down model development at Ubiquiti:

• 
unpredictable real-world environments make it hard to know which data to train on

 auto-annotations aren't precise enough to trust, so data gets re-annotated or scrapped
